title: Dooars rhino loop by train and jeep
start: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport
end: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport

Homestays and budget lodges, 6 nights with dinner and breakfast

meta_description: 6 nights in the Dooars by train and shared jeep: Gorumara, Samsing's tea slopes and Jaldapara's rhinos in homestays, from ₹13,000 per person.
summary: A backpacker's loop through the Dooars using trains, buses and shared jeeps: two nights at Lataguri for Gorumara, two at Samsing in the tea hills, and two at Madarihat for Jaldapara's rhinos. Homestays throughout and shared safari seats keep the daily spend under ₹2,000.
intro: You do not need a private car to see the Dooars. The Dooars line runs from NJP through Malbazar, Chalsa and Madarihat, buses connect every town on the highway, and shared jeeps climb to the hill villages each morning. This loop strings those together into six nights, with homestays at every stop and shared seats in safari jeeps.

The order matters. Gorumara first, close to Siliguri, for watchtower safaris; then up to Samsing for two cool nights among tea and the river valleys of Rocky Island and Suntalekhola; then east to Jaldapara, the biggest rhino park in the region, before the train back to NJP. Expect some waiting at jeep stands; that is part of the price.
highlights: Gorumara watchtowers at dawn and dusk
Two cool nights in Samsing's tea garden
Rocky Island and the Suntalekhola hanging bridge
A dawn jeep safari among Jaldapara's rhinos
The Dooars line train through tea gardens and forest

days.title: NJP to Lataguri, first watchtower
days.drive: ≈ 80 km · 2.5–3.5 h by train or bus
days.text: Take a morning Dooars line train to New Mal Junction or a bus from Siliguri towards Malbazar, then a local auto to Lataguri. Check into a family homestay. In the afternoon, take your pre-booked shared seat on a Gorumara watchtower slot at Jatraprasad or the Rhino Observation Point, where rhinos and gaur visit the salt lick near sunset. Dinner with your hosts, who will usually know which towers have had sightings.

days.title: Murti river and Chapramari
days.text: Sleep in or walk a tea garden road at dawn. Late morning, share an auto or local car to the Murti river and watch the forest department's elephants being bathed at Dhupjhora if you are early enough. In the afternoon, take a shared seat on the Chapramari watchtower slot for gaur at the forest waterhole, or skip it to save money and spend the evening on the Murti riverbed instead. Back to Lataguri for dinner.

days.title: Up into the tea hills at Samsing
days.drive: ≈ 40 km · 2–3 h by bus and shared jeep
days.text: Take a bus or auto from Lataguri to Malbazar and on to Chalsa, then a shared jeep up through Metali to Samsing; jeeps leave when full, so start by mid-morning. The road climbs from the plains into tea, and the air cools as you reach about 900 m. Check into a homestay, have a late lunch and walk the garden roads in the afternoon, looking south over the Dooars plain.

days.title: Rocky Island and Suntalekhola on foot
days.text: Walk down to Rocky Island on the Murti, a few kilometres below Samsing, and sit on the giant boulders by the river; do not swim. Walk back up and continue along the quiet 5 km road to Suntalekhola, crossing the hanging footbridge over the orange stream and watching forktails and redstarts on the rocks. Share a local car back to Samsing if your legs are tired. Dinner of gundruk soup and squash in your homestay kitchen.

days.title: Down to Madarihat for Jaldapara
days.drive: ≈ 90 km · 3–4 h by shared jeep and train or bus
days.text: Take the morning shared jeep from Samsing down to Chalsa. From Chalsa, catch a Dooars line train or a bus east through Nagrakata, Banarhat and Birpara to Madarihat. Check into a homestay or budget lodge near the highway. In the evening, confirm your next morning's shared jeep safari at the forest counter and buy snacks for the early start.

days.title: Dawn rhinos in Jaldapara
days.text: Board your shared jeep for the first safari slot, around 6 am in winter, and drive into the tall grass when rhinos are grazing in the open; Jaldapara has around 330, the most in India after Kaziranga. Back for breakfast and a rest. In the afternoon, walk around Madarihat and the edge of the tea gardens, or share a car to Totopara if a group forms, visiting quietly and respectfully. Early dinner.

days.title: Train back through the gardens to NJP
days.drive: ≈ 125 km · 4–5 h by train or bus
days.text: Take a morning train from Madarihat or Hasimara back west along the Dooars line, through tea gardens and forest edges, to Siliguri Junction or NJP. If the timing does not suit, buses run from Madarihat to Siliguri through the day. Allow a buffer of several hours before any long-distance train or flight from NJP or Bagdogra.

includes: Train, bus and shared jeep fares for the full loop
Six nights in homestays and budget lodges with dinner and breakfast
Three shared safari seats with entry, guide and vehicle fees (Gorumara x1, Jaldapara x1, one more of your choice)
excludes: Totopara car, camera fees and elephant safari
save_money: Ask homestay hosts to put you in touch with other guests to share safari jeeps and local cars.
Use the Dooars line train for the long legs; it is far cheaper than buses or cars and often more comfortable.
Skip the Chapramari slot and spend the evening free on the Murti riverbed if the budget is tight.
good_to_know: Parks close from about 16 June to 15 September; check current status before you travel.
Shared jeeps up to Samsing run mostly in the morning; start early.
Carry cash; ATMs in Lataguri, Samsing and Madarihat are unreliable.
Book safari seats online early; winter weekends sell out.

faqs.q: Can I travel around the Dooars without a car?
faqs.a: Yes. The Dooars line train, highway buses and shared jeeps to the hill villages connect every stop on this loop. It takes more time and some waiting, but costs a fraction of a car. Plan legs for the morning, when services are frequent.

faqs.q: How much does a week in the Dooars cost on a budget?
faqs.a: About ₹13,000 per person for six nights on this plan, roughly ₹1,850 a day, including homestays with meals, transport and three shared safari seats. Add a few thousand for extra safaris, Totopara or a private jeep.

faqs.q: Is this trip good for solo travellers?
faqs.a: Very good. Homestays happily take single guests, shared jeeps and trains suit solo budgets, and other guests are often keen to share safari jeeps. Single-room supplements are small or nil in many homestays. Keep to daylight travel.

faqs.q: How reliable are shared jeeps to Samsing?
faqs.a: They run from Chalsa and Metali several times a day, mostly in the morning, leaving when full. Afternoon departures are fewer. If you miss one, a local car to Samsing costs roughly ₹800–1,200, which you can share.

faqs.q: Which is better for rhinos, Gorumara or Jaldapara?
faqs.a: Jaldapara has about five times as many rhinos and open grassland, so sightings are more likely. Gorumara's watchtowers often give closer, calmer views at the salt licks. This loop includes both for the best chance.

faqs.q: Can we do the loop in reverse?
faqs.a: Yes. Start with Jaldapara, then Samsing, then Lataguri, finishing close to Siliguri. Train timings may decide the direction. Ending in Lataguri means a shorter final leg back to NJP before your onward journey.

faqs.q: What should a backpacker pack for the Dooars?
faqs.a: A light daypack, layers for cold dawns and warm days, a rain jacket, sturdy shoes, a torch, a power bank, binoculars, insect repellent, a water bottle and cash. Muted colours for safaris. ID for safari bookings.

faqs.q: Are there hostels in the Dooars?
faqs.a: Few or none in the backpacker hostel sense. Homestays with dinner and breakfast at ₹1,200–1,800 per person fill that role and are better value. Forest corporation tents at Murti and Suntalekhola are another cheap option.

faqs.q: Is it safe to travel by train in the Dooars?
faqs.a: Yes. Trains are slow and can be crowded on market days, but are generally safe. Keep bags close, check the timetable the day before and avoid arriving at small stations after dark without a pickup arranged.
